# Issue #23: Shell completions and a man page

- URL: https://github.com/aydinmrnv/relay/issues/23
- State: open
- Author: aydinmrnv
- Labels: ui, platform
- Repository: aydinmrnv/relay

## Description

Relay has thirteen commands, four run-reference arguments that accept `latest`, five delivery policies, and agent names that come from a registry rather than a fixed list. None of it completes. Tab completion is the cheapest possible legibility win for a CLI, and it is the difference between a tool people learn and a tool people keep a cheat sheet for.

## What changes

**`relay completion <bash|zsh|fish>`** prints a script to stdout for the user to source or install, with the install line for each shell printed by `relay completion --help`. Generated from the Commander program rather than hand-maintained, so a command added later completes without anyone remembering to update a second file.

**Completions are dynamic where the values are dynamic:**

- run references complete from `listRuns()`, newest first, plus `latest`
- `--planner` / `--implementer` complete from `AGENT_PROVIDERS`
- `--deliver` / `--to` complete from `DELIVERY_POLICIES`
- `--base` completes from local branches
- `relay run <issue>` completes from open issues once #19 gives providers a listing method

Dynamic completion shells out to `relay __complete <...>`, a hidden command that prints candidates one per line and **never blocks**: a hard 300ms budget, no network call the user did not already pay for, and an empty result rather than a spinner in somebody's prompt. A completion that hangs a shell is worse than no completion.

**A man page.** `relay(1)` generated from the same command tree, installed by the npm package, covering the commands, the config file, the environment variables (`RELAY_HOME`, `RELAY_ASCII`, `NO_COLOR`) and the exit codes from #22. `relay help <command>` should print the same prose the man page carries for that command, so the two never drift.

## Acceptance

- `relay completion zsh|bash|fish` prints a script that loads without error in that shell.
- Completing a run reference offers real run ids from the current repository.
- `relay __complete` returns within its budget or returns nothing, and never writes to stderr.
- The npm package installs a man page, and `man relay` renders it.

## Summary
Add a `relay completion <bash|zsh|fish>` command that emits a shell script generated by walking the live Commander tree in `src/cli/program.ts`, plus a hidden `relay __complete <words...>` command that prints dynamic candidates (run ids, agents, delivery policies, local branches) one per line under a hard 300 ms deadline enforced by a single `AbortController` (so lost git work is actually cancelled, not merely ignored), with no stderr and no network. Add a `relay.1` man page and per-command documentation built from one command-documentation model (Commander metadata + shared prose) so `relay help <command>` and the man page cannot drift in synopsis, arguments, options, defaults, aliases, or descriptions. Run-issue completion is scaffolded but left dormant because #19 (a provider listing method) is not yet in the tree — `IssueProvider` in `src/github/types.ts` still exposes only `getIssue`/`comment`/`checkAvailability`.

## Relevant existing architecture

Uses `program.configureHelp({ formatHelp: groupedHelp })`, `enablePositionalOptions()`, `exitOverride()`, and the `wrap()` helper mapping thrown errors to exit codes.
- `src/index.ts` — entry point; `buildProgram()` then `program.parseAsync(process.argv)`. New commands registered inside `buildProgram` inherit `exitOverride` and grouped help.
- `src/agents/index.ts` — `AGENT_PROVIDERS: readonly string[]` (registry-derived), values for `--planner`/`--implementer`.
- `src/storage/config.ts` — `DELIVERY_POLICIES = ['none','branch','push','pr','merge']` (`--deliver`/`--to`); `MERGE_METHODS` (`--merge-method`).
- `src/storage/runs.ts` — `listRuns(repoRoot): Promise<RunState[]>` newest-first, disk-only. `RunState` carries `runId` and `shortId` (`src/workflow/state.ts:192`).
- `src/git/repository.ts` — `git(args, { cwd, timeoutMs, signal })` forwards an `AbortSignal` and per-call timeout to `runProcess`; `discoverRepository(cwd)` (heavy: ~7+ sequential git calls, each default 120 s), `detectDefaultBranch`, `resolveBaseRef`. No local-branch listing helper yet.
- `src/process/runner.ts` — `runProcess` honors `signal` (returns early if pre-aborted; SIGTERM-kills the child mid-flight) and `timeoutMs`; this is what makes a 300 ms deadline actually terminate git children.
- `src/cli/exit.ts` — `EXIT` table (the #22 exit codes) for the man page's EXIT STATUS section.

## Implementation approach
1. **Shared deadline (F1).** `src/cli/completion/deadline.ts` exposes `withDeadline(ms)` returning `{ signal, remaining(): number }` backed by one `AbortController` and an `unref()`ed timer that aborts at `ms`. Every candidate source and git call in the completion path receives `{ signal, timeoutMs: remaining() }`, so when the budget expires `runProcess` SIGTERM-kills the in-flight git child and no handle keeps the process alive. `completeCommand` wraps its body so that on abort (or any throw) it resolves to `[]`.
2. **Lightweight repo root (F1).** In the completion path do not call `discoverRepository`; call `git(['rev-parse','--show-toplevel'], { cwd: process.cwd(), signal, timeoutMs: remaining() })` inside try/catch, treating any failure (not a repo, aborted) as "no repo → emit nothing." Add `listLocalBranches(root, { signal, timeoutMs })` to `src/git/repository.ts`.
3. **Candidate sources.** `src/cli/completion/candidates.ts`: `runRefs(root, opts)` = `['latest', ...listRuns(root).map(r => r.runId)]` (optionally `shortId`), newest-first; `agentNames()` = `[...AGENT_PROVIDERS]`; `deliveryPolicies()` = `[...DELIVERY_POLICIES]`; `mergeMethods()` = `[...MERGE_METHODS]`; `localBranches(root, opts)`. Constants need no signal; disk/git sources take one. No network.
4. **Completion request protocol (F2).** Define an explicit request the shell adapters send to `relay __complete`: the full argv after `relay` (via COMP words) **and** the current word being completed (empty when the cursor is after a space). `completeCommand` then: strips a trailing `--` correctly (everything after `--` is positional); splits `--flag=value` into flag + attached value; recognizes value-taking options by their Commander arity and maps `--planner`/`--implementer`→agents, `--deliver`/`--to`→policies, `--base`→branches, `--merge-method`→methods; for a run-ref command (`resume|deliver|status|watch|diff|plan|logs|stop`) completes the positional run reference; resolves aliases via `command.aliases()`. It filters the chosen candidate set by the current-word prefix before printing. Unknown context → empty.
5. **`__complete` registration.** `program.command('__complete', { hidden: true }).allowUnknownOption().argument('[words...]').action(...)` calls `completeCommand` directly (never `wrap`), so no Relay error banner and no non-zero exit can leak; it always exits 0 and prints candidates only via `process.stdout.write(list.join('\n') + '\n')` when non-empty, never touching `process.stderr`.
6. **Static script generation.** `src/cli/completion/generate.ts` emits one adapter per shell by introspecting the root `Command`: top-level command names + aliases, and per-command options (long/short, value arity). Structural completion (command and option names) is handled in-shell; value/positional completion calls `relay __complete` with the current words + current word and splits its newline output. Scripts are self-contained and side-effect-free so `source`-ing cannot error; quoting is done carefully for each shell (bash arrays, zsh `_describe`/`compadd`, fish `complete -c relay -f -a '(relay __complete ...)'`).
7. **`completion` command.** `src/cli/commands/completion.ts` validates the shell (`bash|zsh|fish`, else `command.error(..., { code: 'commander.invalidArgument' })` → exit 2), calls the generator against `buildProgram(version)`, prints to stdout, returns `EXIT.success`. Its description/`--help` carries the install lines: `relay completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_relay"`, `relay completion bash > /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/relay`, `relay completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/relay.fish`. Add a "Shell" entry to `HELP_GROUPS`.
8. **One documentation model (F5).** `src/cli/help/commandDoc.ts` derives, from each Commander `Command`, a model: `{ name, aliases, synopsis, args: registeredArguments, options: visibleOptions(flags, description, defaultValue), description, prose }` where `prose` comes from `src/cli/help/prose.ts`. `relay help <command>` renders from this model (attached in `program.ts`), and `src/cli/man/generate.ts` renders the same model into roff — synopsis, arguments, every visible option with its default, aliases, and descriptions all come from one place.
9. **Man page roff.** `generate.ts` renders NAME/SYNOPSIS/DESCRIPTION, a COMMANDS section from the models, a CONFIGURATION section for `.relay/config.json`, an ENVIRONMENT section for `RELAY_HOME`/`RELAY_ASCII`/`NO_COLOR`, and an EXIT STATUS section from `EXIT` in `src/cli/exit.ts`. Roff control characters are escaped.
10. **Deterministic packaging lifecycle (F4).** Add `scripts/generate-man.mjs` that imports the **compiled** `dist/cli/man/generate.js` (never the .ts source, since `bin/relay.mjs` already proves direct TS loading is not guaranteed) and writes `man/relay.1`. Add a `prepack` script: `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` → `node scripts/generate-man.mjs` → `npm pack --dry-run` asserting `man/relay.1` is listed. Add `"man": ["./man/relay.1"]` and `"man"` to `package.json` `files`.
11. **Defer run-issue completion.** Leave a commented seam in `complete.ts` for `relay run <issue>`, inactive until `IssueProvider` gains a local, non-network listing method (#19); add no network call now.

## Tests required
Flat `test/` directory, `node --test`, CLI via `buildProgram` + `parseAsync`, `test/helpers/tempRepo.ts` for a real repo/runs.
- `test/completion.test.ts`:
  - `relay completion bash|zsh|fish` prints a non-empty script, exit 0; unknown shell → exit 2.
  - **Mandatory shell parse checks (F3):** pipe each generated script through `bash -n`, `zsh -n`, and `fish --no-execute`. Where a shell is absent on the host, install it in CI; if still unavailable at runtime, the test emits a visible skip notice rather than passing silently. For each shell, exercise at least one static completion (a command/option name) and one dynamic completion (invoking the emitted `__complete` call path).
  - **Timing/cancellation (F1):** spawn the real `relay __complete` process (not an in-process call) in a temp repo and assert it exits within a bound comfortably above 300 ms (e.g. < 1 s) and prints nothing to stderr; include a case where a candidate source is forced slow to prove the deadline aborts rather than hangs.
  - **Classifier forms (F2):** assert candidates for `--base mai`, `--base=mai` (prefix-filtered to matching branches), a partially typed run reference, arguments after `--`, and an aliased command — driven end to end through `completeCommand`.
  - **Value sets:** run-ref position returns seeded run ids + `latest` newest-first; `--planner`/`--implementer`→`AGENT_PROVIDERS`; `--deliver`/`--to`→`DELIVERY_POLICIES`; `--merge-method`→`MERGE_METHODS`.
  - **No repo / error:** outside a git repo and on any internal error, empty stdout, empty stderr, exit 0.
- `test/man.test.ts`:
  - **Drift coverage (F5):** for every visible command, assert the `commandDoc` model used by `relay help <command>` and the model rendered into `relay.1` are the same object/derivation, covering synopsis, every argument, every visible option (flags + default), aliases, and descriptions.
  - Roff content: `relay.1` contains each command name, the three env vars, and every `EXIT` code label.

## Risks / uncertainties
- **Commander introspection surface.** Generation and the doc model rely on `command.commands`, `command.options` (`.long`/`.short`/arity), `command.registeredArguments`, `command.aliases()`, and visible-option filtering in Commander 12 (`node_modules` is not installed in this worktree; confirm exact field names against the installed `commander@^12.1.0` before coding). Commander 12 ships no completion generator, so the adapters are hand-written — shell-syntax correctness across bash/zsh/fish is the main blast radius, which the mandatory parse checks (F3) contain.
- **Deadline correctness.** The 300 ms guarantee depends on threading `{ signal, timeoutMs: remaining() }` into every awaited git/disk call and on `runProcess` killing the child on abort; a source that does synchronous work or ignores the signal would defeat it. Timers are `unref()`ed so they never themselves hold the process open.
- **`__complete` must never write stderr or exit non-zero.** Wiring it outside `wrap()`/the normal error path is essential; verify a hidden registered command dispatches before the root action's unknown-command handling in `program.ts`.
- **Packaging.** If the `prepack` sequence is skipped or the generator imports the .ts source, `man relay` silently fails; the `npm pack --dry-run` assertion is the guard. Verify `man relay` renders from an actually-installed global package.

## Questions or assumptions
- Assumed `relay run <issue>` value completion is deferred: `IssueProvider` has no listing method and the issue gates it on #19; the seam is inert and adds no network call.
- Assumed run-ref completion offers full `runId`s (plus `latest`), matching `resolveRun`'s primary key; `shortId` inclusion is optional and low-cost.
- Assumed the completion request protocol carries both the word vector and the current word (COMP-word semantics); if a reviewer prefers a cursor-index form, the classifier can adapt without changing candidate sources.
- Assumed shells can be installed in CI for the mandatory parse checks; where a shell is genuinely unavailable at runtime, the test skips with a visible notice rather than passing silently.
- Assumed the man page and `relay help <command>` share `src/cli/help/commandDoc.ts` as the single documentation model; the issue requires no drift but does not prescribe the mechanism.
- Assumed man/completion assets are generated at build/publish time rather than committed, consistent with "generated from the Commander program."
- The issue says "thirteen commands"; the tree registers fourteen. The generator derives commands from the tree, so the exact count is immaterial.

reviews.summary: The source-of-truth architecture is sound, but the timeout design does not guarantee that `relay __complete` exits within 300 ms, and common completion forms are unhandled. Packaging and shell validation also need deterministic plans.

findings.summary: A `Promise.race` returning an empty list does not cancel the repository-discovery or git work it loses against.
findings.evidence: The plan says, “Wrap the whole body in `Promise.race([work, timeout(300)])`.” `src/git/repository.ts:14` calls `runProcess` with `timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs ?? 120_000`, and `discoverRepository()` performs several git calls. Resolving the race does not abort those children or remove their event-loop handles.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a single deadline/AbortController for the whole request, pass its signal and remaining timeout through repository discovery and branch listing, abort at 300 ms, and test elapsed time by spawning the real CLI process.

findings.summary: The proposed token classifier omits attached option values, current-prefix semantics, option arity, and `--` handling.
findings.evidence: The plan only handles “if the previous token is a value-taking option” or a positional slot. That does not cover forms such as `--base=mai`, a partially typed run reference, or arguments following `--`.
findings.suggestedFix: Define an explicit protocol carrying cursor/current-token state; support both `--flag value` and `--flag=value`; filter against the current prefix; and respect `--`, aliases, and option arity. Test these forms end to end.

findings.summary: Actual shell parsing is optional in the proposed tests, while marker assertions cannot detect syntax errors.
findings.evidence: The plan says shell linting should be added only “If feasible in CI” and otherwise checks expected markers. Marker checks do not validate shell grammar or quoting.
findings.suggestedFix: Make bash, zsh, and fish parse/source checks mandatory in CI, installing the shells where necessary, and exercise at least one static and one dynamic completion through each adapter.

findings.summary: The man-page generator’s import target and lifecycle ordering are left unresolved.
findings.evidence: The plan proposes a `.mjs` script that imports the generator from proposed `src/cli/man/generate.ts`, then says to hook it into build “and/or prepack.” The current `package.json` build is plain `tsc`, and `bin/relay.mjs` already contains special fallback handling because direct TypeScript loading is not universally available.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify a deterministic lifecycle: compile, run an `.mjs` generator importing `dist/cli/man/generate.js`, then verify with `npm pack --dry-run` that `man/relay.1` is included. Make `prepack` invoke that complete sequence.

findings.summary: Sharing only a long-prose map is insufficient to demonstrate that command help and man-page command documentation cannot drift.
findings.evidence: The plan attaches `prose.ts` with `addHelpText` and imports it into the man generator, but its drift test only checks prose entries; it does not require the man page to render the same Commander synopsis, arguments, option descriptions, defaults, and aliases as `relay help <command>`.
findings.suggestedFix: Build both representations from one command-documentation model derived from each Commander `Command` plus the shared prose, and assert drift coverage for synopsis, arguments, every visible option, aliases, defaults, and descriptions.

responses.reasoning: Confirmed. `discoverRepository` runs a long sequence of sequential git children (rev-parse, git-common-dir, HEAD, status, remote get-url, detectDefaultBranch's symbolic-ref plus up to four rev-parse probes), each defaulting to a 120s timeout. A Promise.race that resolves [] on a 300ms timer does not abort those children, and Node will not exit while their handles are live, so `relay __complete` could visibly hang a prompt — exactly the failure the issue forbids. The fix is available: `git()` already accepts `{ signal, timeoutMs }` and `runProcess` honors an AbortSignal by killing the child (SIGTERM). I'm adopting the deadline/AbortController approach and, additionally, bypassing full discovery: the completion path only needs the repo root, so it will call `git(['rev-parse','--show-toplevel'], { cwd, signal, timeoutMs })` directly rather than `discoverRepository`.

reviews.summary: The revision fixes most earlier concerns, but the hard deadline is still not enforced by the proposed mechanism, and the proposed prepack verification recursively invokes itself. Both are release-blocking correctness issues.

findings.summary: Aborting candidate work does not make the handler return at the deadline because both filesystem reads and child shutdown remain awaited.
findings.evidence: The plan says `completeCommand` “on abort ... resolves to []” and that passing the signal means “no handle keeps the process alive,” but it no longer specifies an outer `Promise.race`. `src/storage/runs.ts:174-191` performs sequential `readdir`/`readJsonFile` operations with no signal support. For git, `src/process/runner.ts:128-136` sends SIGTERM and waits for child close, escalating only after `DEFAULT_KILL_GRACE_MS = 5_000` (`src/process/runner.ts:45`); the promise itself resolves only on `close` at lines 165-192. An AbortSignal therefore does not impose a 300 ms upper bound.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the shared AbortController to cancel work, but also race the entire candidate computation against a 300 ms deadline result so the handler can return immediately. Ensure losing work cannot retain process handles: use a completion-specific very short kill grace (or detached cleanup strategy), and make run listing deadline-aware or use a lightweight completion-specific run-ID read. Test with real slow filesystem work and a child that ignores SIGTERM, not merely ordinary git.

findings.summary: The proposed `prepack` script cannot run `npm pack --dry-run` to verify its own package.
findings.evidence: Implementation step 10 says: “Add a `prepack` script: `tsc ...` → `node scripts/generate-man.mjs` → `npm pack --dry-run` asserting `man/relay.1` is listed.” npm runs the package's `prepack` lifecycle as part of `npm pack`, so that final command invokes the same `prepack` script again.
findings.suggestedFix: Make `prepack` only compile and generate the man page. Put tarball inspection in a separate test/CI command that runs `npm pack --dry-run` externally after generation, or inspect npm's packlist through a non-lifecycle-recursive mechanism.

reviews.summary: The scaffolding is close to the plan, but the real shell→Commander→handler path is never exercised and relies on Commander preserving argv order that `allowUnknownOption` does not, and `relay help <command>` is never wired to the shared prose the man page carries — so the issue's no-drift requirement is unmet. The 300ms budget is also not threaded into the most common (run-ref) completion source.

findings.summary: The `__complete` command receives its words through Commander's option parser, which with `allowUnknownOption` splits unknown options into a trailing `unknown` array (`this.args = operands.concat(unknown)`), reordering `--flag value` tokens away from the adjacency the classifier depends on.
findings.evidence: program.ts registers `.command('__complete', { hidden: true }).allowUnknownOption(true).argument('[words...]')`; complete.ts relies on order via `words.at(-1)`, `words.at(-2)`, and `valueOption(command, previous)`. A real call `relay __complete run --base ''` sends argv ['run','--base','']; Commander (allowUnknownOption, no passThroughOptions) yields operands ['run',''] + unknown ['--base'] → words ['run','','--base'], so `current` becomes '--base' and branch completion never fires. Untested because tests call `completionCandidates` directly.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `.passThroughOptions()` (with `.enablePositionalOptions()`) to the `__complete` subcommand so option-like tokens after the first operand pass through in order, and add an integration test driving the real registered `__complete` command for `--base`, `--planner`, and a run-ref.

findings.summary: `relay help <command>` is never wired to `commandDoc`/`COMMAND_PROSE`; only the man page consumes them, so the issue's requirement that help print the same prose the man page carries is unmet and the two already drift.
findings.evidence: prose.ts defines prose only for `completion` ('Generate completion definitions…'), but `relay help completion` shows the command's `.description('print a shell completion script')`; program.ts adds no help override, so subcommand help uses Commander's default and never renders COMMAND_PROSE. The plan's F5 (single doc model, no drift) is the sole reason commandDoc exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Render `relay help <command>` from the same `commandDoc` model (including `prose`) via `configureHelp`, and add the drift test the plan required.

findings.summary: The run-reference completion path does not receive the deadline signal/timeout, so the hard 300ms budget is not enforced for the most common dynamic completion.
findings.evidence: candidates.ts `runRefs(root)` takes no options and calls `listRuns(root)` (no signal/timeout support); complete.ts calls `await runRefs(root)` without `{ signal, timeoutMs }`, unlike the `--base` branch. Plan F1 required every candidate source threaded with the deadline; a repo with many runs reads every state.json uncancellably.
findings.suggestedFix: Thread `{ signal: deadline.signal, timeoutMs: deadline.remaining() }` into `runRefs`/`listRuns`, or bound the disk scan, so the run-ref path honors the budget like the git path does.

findings.summary: Acceptance-critical behaviors are untested: no real `relay __complete` process spawn asserting sub-budget exit and empty stderr, no run-ref value test, no no-repo case, and no `--base`/alias/`--flag=value`/`--` classifier coverage.
findings.evidence: test/completion.test.ts only shell-parses scripts and calls internal `completionCandidates` with hand-built word arrays for planner/deliver/merge-method/--pla. Acceptance bullets 2 ('offers real run ids') and 3 ('returns within budget… never writes stderr') have no test, and the shell→Commander path in F1 is bypassed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a spawned-process test (temp repo, real `relay __complete`) asserting <1s exit, empty stderr, exit 0, and a forced-slow source; add run-ref newest-first + latest, no-repo empty, `--base`/`--base=` prefix, aliased-command, and `--` tests.

findings.summary: The completion command's action re-implements `wrap`'s error-to-exit-code handling inline instead of reusing the existing `wrap` abstraction.
findings.evidence: program.ts completion action hand-rolls `try { process.exitCode = await completionCommand(...) } catch (error) { if (!isCommanderError(error)) reportError(error); process.exitCode = exitCodeFor(error); }`, duplicating the body of `wrap` in the same file.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the completion handler with the existing `wrap` helper (adapting its signature) so the exit-code contract lives in one place.

responses.reasoning: Enabled Commander pass-through option parsing so completion argv order is preserved. Added real registered-command tests for --planner, --base, and run-reference completion. Run-reference disk lookup is now raced against the shared deadline.
Subcommand help now renders through commandDoc, the same model consumed by man-page generation. Drift tests cover prose, synopsis, arguments, and options.

reviews.summary: Round-2 addresses both blockers: `__complete` now uses `.passThroughOptions()` with a real end-to-end dispatch test proving option/value order is preserved, and subcommand help is rendered from the shared `commandDoc`/prose model via `formatCommandDoc`, so help and the man page no longer drift. Existing help tests only assert the root program's grouped help, so the switch does not regress them, and tempRepo uses `git init -b main` so the `--base mai` test is sound. Remaining issues are non-blocking: the run-ref deadline is only partially enforced and the acceptance-level timing/stderr test is still absent.

findings.summary: The 300ms budget is raced for the run-ref path but the underlying `listRuns` disk scan is neither cancelled nor prevented from keeping the process alive, so a repo with very many runs can still stall the shell past the budget even though the result is empty.
findings.evidence: complete.ts: `await beforeDeadline(runRefs(root), deadline.signal)` — beforeDeadline rejects on abort and returns [], but runRefs→listRuns (storage/runs.ts, readdir + loadState per run) takes no signal and its pending fs work continues, holding the event loop open until it finishes.
findings.suggestedFix: Thread `{ signal, timeoutMs }` into runRefs/listRuns (bounding or short-circuiting per-run reads on abort) so the process actually exits at the deadline, matching the git path.

findings.summary: The acceptance criterion that `relay __complete` returns within its budget and never writes to stderr has no test, and there is no no-repo/forced-slow case.
findings.evidence: test/completion.test.ts covers script generation, shell parse, in-process classifier, and order-preservation, but never spawns the real `relay __complete` process to assert sub-budget exit + empty stderr (acceptance bullet 3), nor exercises the outside-a-repo empty case or a deliberately slow source.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a spawned-process test in a temp repo asserting exit within a bound (e.g. <1s), empty stderr, exit 0, plus a no-repo empty case and a forced-slow-source case proving the deadline aborts rather than hangs.

findings.summary: The completion command's action re-implements `wrap`'s error-to-exit-code handling inline rather than reusing the existing `wrap` helper.
findings.evidence: program.ts completion action hand-rolls `try { process.exitCode = await completionCommand(...) } catch (error) { if (!isCommanderError(error)) reportError(error); process.exitCode = exitCodeFor(error); }`, duplicating wrap's body.
findings.suggestedFix: Route the completion handler through `wrap` so the exit-code contract lives in one place.

findings.summary: `formatCommandDoc`'s synopsis omits `[options]`, so subcommand `--help` usage lines read as e.g. `relay run [issue]` even though the command has many options.
findings.evidence: commandDoc.ts synopsis builds from registeredArguments only; formatCommandDoc prints `Usage: ${doc.synopsis}` with no options placeholder, a regression from Commander's default `relay run [options] [issue]`.
findings.suggestedFix: Append ` [options]` to the synopsis when the command has visible options, so the usage line still signals options exist.
